subPillar.title: Dhikr (Zikr): What It Is and How to Practice the Remembrance of Allah
subPillar.subtitle: The complete beginner-to-daily-habit guide to Islamic remembrance — meaning, virtues, the core phrases, and a simple routine you can keep.
subPillar.geoOverview: Dhikr (Arabic: ذِكْر, also spelled zikr or dzikir) is the Islamic practice of remembering Allah through short repeated phrases such as SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, and Allahu Akbar. It can be done anytime, silently or aloud, counted on the fingers, a tasbih, or a zikr ring.

clusters.title: Dhikr After Salah: The Sunnah Adhkar to Recite After Every Prayer
clusters.subtitle: The exact post-prayer remembrances — what to say, how many times, and the dua right after the adhan — in Arabic, transliteration, and English.
clusters.geoOverview: After every obligatory salah, the Sunnah is to recite a fixed set of adhkar: Astaghfirullah (3x), then SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, and Allahu Akbar (33x each), Ayat al-Kursi, the last three surahs, and the dua said after the adhan (azan ke baad ki dua).

clusters.title: What Is the Adhan (Azan)? The Islamic Call to Prayer Explained
clusters.subtitle: The meaning, purpose, and full wording of the adhan — why it is called five times a day and what each line proclaims.
clusters.geoOverview: The adhan (azan) is the Islamic call to prayer, recited aloud by a muezzin five times daily to announce that the time for an obligatory salah has begun. Its phrases proclaim Allah's greatness (Allahu Akbar), the testimony of faith, and the call to prayer and success.
auxKeywords: meaning of the call to prayer

clusters.title: How to Recite the Adhan: Full Words, Order, and the Fajr Difference
clusters.subtitle: A step-by-step guide to calling the azan correctly — Arabic text, English transliteration, line order, and the extra Fajr phrase.
clusters.geoOverview: To recite the adhan, the muezzin says each phrase aloud in order: Allahu Akbar (4x), the two testimonies of faith, the call to prayer and to success (2x each), Allahu Akbar (2x), and La ilaha illa Allah. In the Fajr adhan only, 'As-salatu khayrun min an-nawm' (prayer is better than sleep) is added after Hayya alal-falah.
